baseline_prompt_en: A photographic scene of an active investigation, caught at the quiet turn when a witness finally gives useful directions. Inside a modest riverside ferry ticket booth after the final crossing, an investigator is seeking information about a case. She interviews the ferry attendant across a narrow scuffed wooden counter. The investigator's visible facial appearance follows the supplied reference: its rounded facial outline, large dark eyes, fine straight brows and soft lips; her hair follows the reference's dark chin-length bob with wispy separated fringe. The fictional role, clothing and circumstances belong to this scene. She wears a plain charcoal jacket over an ivory shirt, her short hair tucked loosely behind one ear, with soft window light bringing a restrained warmth to her face and the small gap at her collar. She is fully engaged in the answer, her lips slightly parted and her brow concentrated. Her left hand holds a large printed portrait photograph upright by its lower corner, turned toward the attendant and obliquely visible to us. Her right hand has paused a pen just above a small open case notebook. The photograph is a clear head-and-shoulders image of a different person, the subject of her inquiry. Beside the notebook lies a simple ferry-landing diagram, its few bold black lines showing a river, one dock and a forked footpath. The attendant, in a worn navy work sweater, leans forward from the opposite side of the counter. His right index fingertip touches the outer branch of that diagram while his other fingers curl clear of the page; his forearm runs continuously back to his own sleeve. He is in mid-explanation, mouth open, eyes on the investigator. Her gaze drops toward the exact place he indicates, and the poised pen shows that his correction has interrupted her earlier note. Their separate hands, the portrait surface, notebook and fingertip contact remain legible together. Through the side window just beyond the attendant, an empty gangway and its shut gate lead down to the river, visibly tying his workplace to the route he describes. Faded ticket slots and a small stack of unused tickets identify the booth. The photograph's emotional center is the investigator absorbing a specific lead from someone who knows this place. A horizontal medium two-shot from the near corner of the counter keeps both faces in three-quarter view and the shared documents large in the lower center. Natural dusk light from the river window mixes with a modest warm desk lamp, giving skin, paper and worn wood tangible texture. Measured depth of field holds both participants and their joined point of attention clear, while the far water softens. The scene feels observed, personal and quietly urgent.
